about: The size spec for Half-Blood Quests: every model the workbench lists gets a size category relative to Percy.
Body height: the torso, head and legs at rest, as perf/bodysize.cjs measures it (arms, weapons, wings, whips, tails, flames and props left out), divided by Percy's.

Headwear is not body (round 9): helmets, crests, plumes, hats, caps, crowns, circlets and horns are left out of the body height, as weapons and wings are. A builder marks them (game/js/entities/proportions.js markHeadwear: userData.headwear on the meshes, a hat slot in people.js and mortals.js), and perf/bodysize.cjs lists them under 'headwear'. Hair, a hood that is the creature's own head (the karpos's straw cowl) and a bird's own feathered crest stay body.
The check: NODE_PATH=/opt/node22/lib/node_modules node percyjackson/perf/bodysize.cjs - '' --check. A model fails when its body x Percy is outside its category's band, or when the head rule fails.

The principles (round 9, the owner; round 10 for adults), applied to every model: (1) Percy and the young heroes, adolescents, are the 'same' reference, and so are the teen campers, Hunters and other kids. (2) Adults read as adults, bigger than Percy but never giants: the 'adult' band, about 1.2-1.3x Percy's body without headwear (round 10; it was 1.1-1.15x in round 9). This covers grown-up humans (mortals, teachers, tourists, adult NPCs and people), the dead (ghosts, shades, keres) and former adults made monstrous (skeleton warriors, spartoi, living statues of people). With a full head of hair an adult measures about 1.25-1.3x; one in a hat or with cropped hair is measured to the skull, about 1.2x (mortals.js ADULT_SCALE_HAT), its skull level with the others'. Helmets, crests and hats included, an adult stands no more than about 1.4x overall. Grown-ups get an adult's smaller head on the same body (mortals.js ADULT_HEAD; the former adults and the ghost by proportions.js reshape). A grown-up the books call short or tiny (Mr. D, Coach Hedge, Grandma Mae) stays about a twelve-year-old's height, 'same', by the owner's earlier ruling. (3) The champions of these adults stand a modest step above them, 'adultChampion', about 1.45-1.55x, not giants. (4) An enemy meant to intimidate outsizes a person even where its book or real-life counterpart is small (the giant scorpion): game drama beats canon. (5) Small fodder still reads clearly at gameplay distance: a swarm creature is no smaller than about 0.75x Percy, its plume aside.

Bigger models get more voxels, not bigger voxels: a model grown with its rig scale is sculpted in cells of a hero's size (parts.js voxDensity, densityFor; proportions.js reshape for a grown body's proportions), and the head and leg rules below apply as it grows.

Categories are given by the role in the game and the drama first (an elite or a boss should loom), with the owner's rulings fixed, the concept sheets and the books as a guide, not a ceiling. Exaggeration is expected: what matters is the relation to Percy.
Source order: owner (an explicit ruling, design/size-audit.md), sheet (the concept sheet's drawing beside its Percy, measured: see sheetMethod), books, role.
test/sizes.test.mjs checks that every workbench model has an entry with a known category and a reason.

categories._note: The one place to tune the bands: body height x Percy, min and max. Neighbouring bands overlap a little, so a model near a border is not flagged for a few centimetres. 'same' runs down to 0.82 (round 9): a teen in a cap or helmet is measured to the skull, the hair it cuts aside. 'adult' (round 9) is a grown-up's band between 'same' and 'slightlyBigger'. Round 10: 'adult' moved to 1.15-1.35 (the owner: grown-ups, the dead and former adults made monstrous all stand about 1.2-1.3x Percy, bigger but never giants; an adult measured to the skull under a hat or cropped hair at its foot), and 'adultChampion', 1.42-1.6, is their champions' modest step above. Both are marked "aside": bands for a class of models beside the ladder of sizes, not steps of it (test/sizes.test.mjs checks the ladder's order and overlaps without them).

adultChampion.label: an adult's champion, a modest step above

head._note: The owner's rule: as characters grow, the Minecraft-style big head gives way to more realistic proportions, but toward each creature's own proportion on its concept sheet, not one size for all (round 8: 'it shouldn't converge to a single size, only toward the proportion in the source image'). For an upright model (a Rig: not a four-legged QuadRig or a serpent), the head is its head block's height (the skull and face where the builder names them, rig.extras.headCore, measured along the head's own axis; else its skin cube) over its body height. A model with a "headSheet" (its sheet's head over body height, read as sheetMethod reads heights: the skull and face, hair, beard, horns and hood aside, over crown to ground) must lie between `ratio` - `tol` and a top that falls in a straight line from `hero` at `from` x Percy to `ratio` at `to` x Percy and over (plus `tol`; tol defaults to `sheetTol`): a mid-sized one is on its way from a hero's head to its sheet's, a big one at its sheet's. A model without one falls back to the general top: at most `hero` at `from` x Percy and under, falling in a straight line to `big` at `to` x Percy and over (plus `tol`). The floor: an upright model of `floorFrom` x Percy or more never has a head smaller than Percy's own, in absolute size. Heroes measure 0.23-0.29; an adult is about 0.13 (7.5 heads tall). A model whose head is a known follow-up has "head": "followUp" with the reason: the check prints it as a warning, not a failure, and says when the mark can go.

legs._note: The owner's leg rule (round 7), beside the head rule: hero-sized Minecraft characters stand on short-ish legs, and as a creature grows its legs approach a real body's. For an upright model (a Rig, not a QuadRig or serpent), its leg length (hip joint to sole, perf/bodysize.cjs) over its body height (sole to crown, hair, horns and hood included) must be at least `hero` at `from` x Percy and under, rising in a straight line to `big` at `to` x Percy and over (less `tol`). Measured this way the heroes read 0.27-0.32 (their hair tops the body; to the top of the skull it is about 0.35-0.38) and a giant at 0.42 or more has legs about half its height to the skull. A model whose legs are hidden or not a person's (a robe to the floor, a hovering Fury in a long dress, a serpent tail) has "legs": "exempt" with the reason in legsNote; a known follow-up has "legs": "followUp" (a warning). QuadRigs record leg root height over shoulder height in the table, unchecked.

sheetMethod: A sheet's ratio is the creature's body height in pixels (crown of the head or hair to the ground it stands on; wings, weapons, flames and raised tails left out) over the height of the Percy figure beside it (crown of his hair to his soles), both read off the image with a pixel ruler (rows of the original 2400 x 1600 PNG). The sheets draw every kind larger than the game does: a person-sized figure on the same sheet (the skeleton and the empousa on vox-enemies, the shades on vox-ow-fodder, the keres on vox-ow-fodder-3) measures about 1.7-1.8x its Percy. So `people` gives that figure's ratio on the sheet and `norm` = ratio / people is the sheet's size in game terms; on vox-ow-fodder `norm` matches the game's karpos, myrmex and crab within 0.1x. The champion and boss sheets draw every figure about 4-4.5x a small running Percy, so only their relative sizes are evidence.
